memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: If cases come before your courts that are too difficult for you to judge—whether bloodshed, lawsuits or assaults—take them to the place the Lord your God will choose. Go to the Levitical priests and to the judge who is in office at that time. Inquire of them and they will give you the verdict. - Deut 17:8-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God knew that some matters would be too hard for local judges to settle. Difficult cases of bloodshed, disputes, or assault needed wiser, more experienced guidance. So God provided a higher court, the priests and the appointed judge at His chosen place. No one was left to struggle alone with matters beyond them.

There is real humility built into this arrangement. Local leaders were expected to admit when a case was beyond their wisdom and to seek help rather than stubbornly forcing a verdict they were unsure of. God does not honour proud independence that refuses counsel.

We can learn from this. Life brings decisions and situations that are simply too complex for us to sort out on our own. God, in His kindness, has surrounded us with wise counsellors, mature believers, pastors, and godly friends who can help us see clearly. Scripture tells us that in an abundance of counsellors there is safety (Prov 11:14). Seeking help is not weakness; it is wisdom. Above all, we have access to God Himself, who gives wisdom generously to all who ask (Jas 1:5). When you face something too difficult to untangle alone, do you turn to wise counsel and to God, or do you insist on managing it by yourself?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you seek wise counsel, or insist on going it alone?
2. Who are the godly counsellors God has placed around you?
3. What difficult situation should you bring to God in prayer today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for the gift of wise counsel and for Your promise of wisdom. Give me humility to seek help when I need it. Amen.
